Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Ruturaj Gaikwad and the local boy, Shubman Gill are the two openers for India.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Australia have posted a fighting total on the board, but their bowlers will need to be absolutely on point to stop the hosts. India will be confident that they have enough quality in their ranks to gun this total down and take an early lead in the series. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

The man of the moment for India, Mohammad Shami, is in for a chat. He says that the pacers enjoy each other's success. Adds that this is the result of them spending the last 7-8 years together. Reckons that with the new ball, he has the responsibility of setting the tempo. Feels that there was not much help from the surface and hence, it was important to use the cutters.

India, on the other hand, was very good with the ball and KL Rahul utilised his assets well but he will be a bit disappointed with his keeping in this game. They played with only five bowlers but that did not affect them that much. Mohammad Shami set the tone by getting rid of Mitchell Marsh early and when the hosts needed a breakthrough, it was him again who dismissed Steven Smith. However, Shreyas Iyer will think that if he hadn't dropped David Warner then they could have restricted the Aussies to a lower total. Ravindra Jadeja got the big wicket of Warner while Ravichandran Ashwin on his comeback got the in-form Marnus Labuschagne which helped India gain control of this game. At the death, they did concede a few boundaries, but Shami ran through the lower middle order of the visitors and registered a fine five-for while Shardul Thakur remained the only one without a wicket in this game.

Australia struggled initially and losing Mitchell Marsh in the very first over did not help either. Steven Smith wasn't able to find his timing right but David Warner looked good and played more freely after getting a life as he went on to register a nice half-century but got out just after which shifted the momentum a bit. They added 94 runs together but the visitors failed to build long partnerships after that as both Smith and Marnus Labuschagne couldn't convert their starts into a big score. Despite their long batting order, they were not that aggressive and it looked like they went into a shell. Cameron Green also got a start but a huge mix-up in the middle with Josh Inglis cost him his wicket. However, a 62-run stand between Inglis and Marcus Stoinis towards the end of the innings took Australia to a competitive score.

A quality bowling performance from India! Mohammad Shami led from the front with a brilliant five-wicket haul which is also the first by any Indian bowler against the Aussies on home soil that helped the hosts restrict Australia to 276. The visitors will be a bit unhappy as looking at their team, they would have hoped for something around or over 300, but their bowlers will like this challenge against this top opposition.

OUT! RUN OUT! Australia have been bowled out on the last ball of their innings! Shardul Thakur bowls full and near the tramline on off, Pat Cummins makes room and has to reach out for the delivery. Carves it towards deep point where Suryakumar Yadav relays the back towards Ravindra Jadeja. The latter fails to pick it up cleanly and the batters think of stealing a third. Jadeja recovers well and fires an accurate throw to KL Rahul at the batting end, who takes the bails off calmly to catch Adam Zampa well short of his crease. Australia end up with 276 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-game formalities. Bright and sunny skies greet the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. They are joined by the Indian players and the two openers for Australia, David Warner and Mitchell Marsh. Mohammad Shami has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Off we go...

We are moments away from the first ball in the series opener, but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players will line up for the national anthems. It will be Australia's national anthem first, followed by the national anthem of India.

Ishan Kishan is in for a chat. He says that it is the beauty of the game that you are not sure where you are going to bat, especially when there are so many good batters in the team. Mentions that when he opens, he looks to be aggressive. Adds that while batting in the middle order, it is important to read the situation. Shares that he enjoys this challenge and the change of batting position does not make a difference to him.

Australia's captain Pat Cummins says that it is good to be back in India. Adds that it has not been too long since they were here. Informs that Mitchell Starc and Glenn Maxwell are unavailable for this game. Mentions that they would have bowed first as well. Adds that they are not too upset since it looks like a pretty good wicket. Also informs that David Warner and Mitchell Marsh will open and that Alex Carey has been rested.

KL Rahul, the skipper of India, says that they will bowl first. Adds that historically this has been a good chasing ground. Tells that there are certain boxes left to tick and they would like to do that playing at home. Mentions Australia are a very competitive team so it will be interesting to face them. With the ODI World Cup less than a fortnight away, there cannot be a better appetiser than a three-match ODI series between two fierce rivals in world cricket, India and Australia. These ODIs will serve as a World Cup dress rehearsal for the two teams that will be facing off in their campaign opener in Chennai. The first of the three ODIs will be played at the Punjab Cricket Association IS Bindra Stadium in Mohali before the action shifts to Indore and Rajkot for the second and third ODIs, respectively. The hosts, India, are riding high on confidence after a successful Asia Cup triumph in Sri Lanka. If the Men in Blue manage to beat Australia with a 2-1 scoreline or better, they will enter the World Cup as the top-ranked ODI side. When it comes to the team setup for this series, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, and Kuldeep Yadav have been rested for the first two ODIs. KL Rahul has been handed the reigns in Rohit's absence for the first couple of ODIs. The squad announcement was headlined by the return of veteran spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, who is being looked at as a potential replacement for the injured Axar Patel in the World Cup squad, as is Washington Sundar. With one of the two opening spots up for grabs, Ruturaj Gaikwad finds a place in the squad, but it seems he will have to wait for his chance in the playing XI. The other option at the top for India is Ishan Kishan, who opened during India's short chase in the Asia Cup final and might get the nod at the top for the first two games alongside Shubman Gill. In all likelihood, Shreyas Iyer will return to his number 4 spot and form the crux of India's batting with KL Rahul and Suryakumar Yadav. Except for the game against Nepal, Ravindra Jadeja was ordinary with the ball by his standards in the Asia Cup and will be eager to regain form ahead of the mega event. As always, India's pace duo of Mohammed Siraj and Jasprit Bumrah will be up for the challenge, making life difficult for batters with the new ball. With the inclusion of Washington Sundar and Ravichandran Ashwin, India's batting depth does not seem an issue for this series, in which case an interesting scenario arises for the third seamer spot between Shardul Thakur and Mohammad Shami. On the other hand, Australia are coming off an ODI series loss against South Africa. Having squandered a 2-0 lead in the five-match series, Pat Cummins' men will be eager to get their World Cup preparations back on track through this series. The Aussie fans will be delighted with the return of skipper Pat Cummins, Steven Smith, Mitchell Starc, and Glenn Maxwell, who missed the tour of South Africa due to injuries. In what has come as a huge setback, Travis Head suffered a fracture to his left hand and now faces a race against time to be fit for the World Cup. In his absence, Mitchell Marsh will slot in at the top of the order alongside David Warner. Having impressed in South Africa, Marnus Labuschagne will hold Australia's batting together with his partner in crime, Steven Smith. Glenn Maxwell is yet to fully recover from his ankle injury and will be unavailable for the first ODI. Despite missing their star-all rounder, there will be no shortage of firepower with the presence of all-rounders Marcus Stoinis and Cameron Green. In the pace department, they will be without the services of Mitchell Starc for the series opener but this is still a potent pace attack consisting of Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood. With Ashton Agar missing from the squad, the spin bowling duties will heavily rest on Adam Zampa, who had a series to forget in South Africa. Earlier this year, these two sides featured in a bilateral series in India, where Australia came from a game down to clinch the three-match ODI series. Do Australia start as favourites?
